=== Morphological Assessment Form ===
A. Leaf Arrangement & Architecture
    1. Leaf relative position (alternate / opposite / whorled): whorled (multiple leaves clearly attached at the same node, visible in multiple images)
    2. Leaf spacing (clustered / distal): clustered (leaves are grouped closely at nodes along the stem)

B. Leaf Complexity
    3. Leaf complexity (simple / compound): simple (each leaf is a single blade without leaflets)
    4. Compound leaf type, ONLY if leaf complexity is compound (odd-pinnate / even-pinnate): N/A
    5. Number of leaflets (integer estimate 2, 4, 8, …): N/A
    6. Leaflet arrangement (opposite / alternate / subopposite): N/A

C. Leaf Morphology
    7. Leaf margin (entire / toothed) AND if toothed (dentate, serrate, etc.)): entire (smooth margin with no teeth or lobes)
    8. Leaf shape (elliptic, obovate, lanceolate, etc.): lanceolate (narrow, tapering to a point, wider at the base)
    9. Leaf apex (acute, obtuse, acuminate): acute (sharply pointed tip)
    10. Leaf base (rounded, cordate, cuneate): cuneate (tapering to a narrow base)
    11. Venation type (pinnate / palmate / parallel): pinnate (main vein with lateral veins branching off)
    12. Secondary veins (visibility, spacing, number): visible, spaced evenly, multiple pairs (clearly visible in multiple images)
    13. Leaf surface features (glabrous, shiny, dull, rugose): shiny (surface reflects light, appears glossy)
    14. Leaf surface trichomes (present / absent): absent (no visible hairs on leaf surface)
    15. Petiole length (short / long): short (petiole is short and not elongated)
    16. Petiole features (winged / grooved / terete): terete (round in cross-section, no wings or grooves)

D. Stem & Shoot Traits
    17. Stem type, may not be visible (woody / herbaceous): woody (stem appears firm and slightly woody, not soft)
    18. Stem trichomes (present / absent): absent (no visible hairs on stem)
    19. Stem color: green to brownish (green at top, transitioning to brownish lower down)
    20. Stem texture (smooth / ridged / lenticellate): smooth (no ridges or lenticels visible)

E. Other Visible Seedling Traits
    21. Stipules, sometimes visible only in close-up images (present / absent): absent (no stipules observed at leaf base)
    22. Latex, rarely visible but extremely diagnostic when present (present / not observed): not observed (no latex visible)
    23. Pulvinus, for Fabaceae family only (present / absent): absent (no pulvinus visible)
    24. Tendrils (present / absent): absent (no tendrils observed)

F. Notes: Some leaves show small holes, likely from minor damage; no clear evidence of herbivory or pathogen. The seedling is marked with pink and orange tags, likely for research purposes. Multiple views confirm whorled leaf arrangement with 5-6 leaves per node. Leaf surface is glossy and smooth, with no trichomes. Stem is slightly woody and smooth. No latex or stipules visible.
